questions.q: (S)-Butan-2-yl tosylate is treated with NaBr in acetone. The product is:
questions.explain: Bromide attacks from the back side in one step and the tosylate leaves, so configuration is inverted (Walden inversion).

questions.q: Which is the correct order of SN2 reactivity?
questions.explain: Bulky groups block back-side attack, so reactivity falls with substitution; tertiary halides show no SN2.

questions.q: An alkyl bromide R–Br is treated separately with AgNO₂ and with KNO₂. The major products are respectively:
questions.explain: The covalent silver salt attacks through N to give the nitroalkane, while the ionic potassium salt attacks through O to give the alkyl nitrite.

questions.q: Neopentyl bromide reacts with NaOH extremely slowly by SN2 even though it is a primary halide. The reason is:
options: The C–Br bond lies in a ring plane
The bulky tert-butyl group blocks the back side of the carbon
Bromide is a poor leaving group
It forms a very stable carbocation instead
questions.explain: SN2 reactivity falls with steric hindrance at the back side; the adjacent tert-butyl group shields the reacting CH₂.
